title: Standardize memory allocator and lightweight timer wheel for scheduler
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent latency spikes and periodic CPU GC-like behavior in the serving runtime under sustained multimodel workloads. Root causes identified in profiling: (1) heterogeneous use of allocators across components (tcmalloc on some CI builds, system malloc on others, and custom arena allocators in the KV layer) causing fragmentation and cross-thread contention; (2) frequent high-resolution timer syscalls from the scheduler's wheel implementation that create syscall overhead and jitter at high QPS; (3) dependency drift around upstream allocator and threading libraries increases maintenance burden.

Objective: Reduce 99th/99.9th latency variance and tail CPU usage by standardizing on a single memory allocator (evaluated: mimalloc vs jemalloc) across the runtime and replacing the current timer implementation with a lightweight, lock-free timer wheel optimized for our slot allocator and batch lanes.

Scope and deliverables:
- Create an allocator abstraction layer and converge runtime builds to the chosen allocator (mimalloc selected in the design doc). Ensure behavior parity on Linux x86_64 and macOS CI images.
- Replace expensive per-request timer syscalls with a compact timer wheel that coalesces wakeups, supports sub-millisecond granularity, and exposes metrics (wheel_len, buckets_in_use, next_tick_latency).
- Update build tooling and container images to include allocator runtime flags and library dependencies.
- Upgrade the threading library dependency to the vetted version that includes necessary futex/condvar fixes (see dependency list in attachments).
- Add integration tests that simulate bursty multimodel traffic and measure allocator fragmentation and timer wakeup counts.
- Rollout plan with canary (10% traffic), metrics dashboard, and auto-rollback on regressions.

Non-goals: Rewriting the KV eviction policy or batcher algorithm. This ticket only touches allocator boundaries and timer/scheduler internals.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: Collected flame graphs from production canaries. Observed allocator hotspots in KV shard and scheduler timer threads. Assigned to Luis.

2026-03-03 - Design meeting: Team decided to standardize on mimalloc due to lower fragmentation in our allocations and smaller binary impact vs. jemalloc on macOS. Action: write allocator abstraction (JIRA-style API) to avoid sprinkling #ifdefs.
2026-03-05 - Spike results: microbenchmarks show mimalloc reduces RSS growth by ~18% under synthetic shard load; timer syscall rate drops 40% when coalescing 1ms ticks into a 4-bucket wheel.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8127 - initial allocator adapter and CI matrix changes (linux/macos). Needs review from infra and build.

2026-03-08 - Code review feedback: infra asked to preserve MALLOC_CONF passthrough for customers that set LD_PRELOAD. Also flagged that ASAN builds should still use the system allocator; added conditional in CMake.

2026-03-09 - Scheduler refactor: Implemented lock-free single-producer multi-consumer wheel ring for timers. Benchmarks: timer wakeups reduced by 62% on 64-lane synthetic workload; tail latency 99.9th reduced by 14% in benchmark harness.

2026-03-10 - Integration test: Found an edge case where timer coalescing delayed slot preemption under very low-latency targets. Mitigation: add an urgent bucket and max-coalesce window of 250us for latency-critical requests.
2026-03-11 - Security review note: allocator change validated by security team for no effect on cryptographic randomness and no new FFI boundaries. Marked security_review_required=false.

2026-03-12 - Plan to rollout: create canary cluster image runtime-2.4-canary-3, enable on Dedicated lower-tier pool, monitor metrics listed in attachments. If RSS or tail latency degrades by >5% for 5m, automatic rollback.
Follow-ups: track memory_profiler leaks (ENG-100001) and extend timer API for cross-process coordination (ENG-100002).
acceptance_criteria: All runtime shards build and pass CI with mimalloc in release and debug modes (ASAN still uses system malloc)
End-to-end canary shows <=0% increase in median latency and <5% regression in 99.9th latency vs baseline within 72h
Timer wakeup syscalls per-second reduced by >=40% in synthetic burst tests
No memory regression (RSS, fragmentation) across a 48h soak on dedicated canary lane
Docs updated: allocator troubleshooting and runtime flags added to Console and Ops runbooks
